title: RBAC v2 Default Role Definitions (Role Matrix + SoD Guidance)
author: Naomi Feldman
body:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s **default RBAC v2 roles** and recommended **SSO group-to-role mapping** for enterprise customers. It is designed to:
- Provide a clear **separation of duties (SoD)** baseline.
- Make permission grants explainable during security reviews and audits (SOC 2 / ISO).
- Reduce misconfiguration during rollout (Hosted, Dedicated, and Private).

This page does **not** describe every individual permission/action; see the Permission Inventory and the policy bundle for the authoritative list.

---

## Scope and terminology
**RBAC v2 primitives (recap)**
- **Resource**: the thing being accessed (e.g., org, project, billing account, audit log export, api key, dedicated pool).
- **Action**: what is being done (e.g., read, update, create, delete, rotate, export).
- **Scope**: where the permission applies (typically **org** or **project**; some operations are global to an org).

**Role assignment scope**
Default roles are assignable at:
- **Org scope** (recommended for enterprise admins): impacts all projects in the org.
- **Project scope** (recommended for developer access): least-privilege per project.

**Policy bundle**
- Default roles are shipped in the RBAC v2 policy bundle (initial GA target: **bundle v0.1**).
- Private deployments may pin bundle versions; confirm your bundle version before relying on any particular permission mapping.

---

## Default roles (summary)
The following default roles are supported across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (availability may vary by tier; see notes under each role).

1) **Org Admin** (high privilege)
2) **Billing Admin** (financial operations only)
3) **Security Admin** (security posture, audit, identity configuration)
4) **Developer** (build and operate application resources; no org-wide admin)
5) **Read-only** (view-only)
6) **Support (Impersonation / Break-glass)** (Redwood internal only; time-bounded)

---

## Role matrix (high-level)
Legend: ✅ allowed by default, ◐ allowed with constraints (see notes), ❌ not allowed

| Capability area | Org Admin | Billing Admin | Security Admin | Developer (Project) | Read-only | Support / Break-glass |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Org settings (name, domains, org metadata) | ✅ | ❌ | ◐ (security-relevant fields only) | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ |
| Membership management (invite/remove users) | ✅ | ❌ | ◐ (invite/remove only to satisfy security controls) | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ |
| Role assignment (grant/revoke roles) | ✅ | ❌ | ◐ (security roles only; see SoD) | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ |
| SSO/SAML/OIDC configuration | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ |
| API keys (create/rotate/revoke) | ◐ (org-wide keys) | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (project-scoped keys) | ❌ | ◐ |
| Model serving configuration (projects, routes, rollouts) | ◐ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ (read) | ◐ |
| Usage analytics (token usage, throughput) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (project only) | ✅ (read) | ✅ |
| Billing (payment method, invoices) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (read-only invoices if enabled) | ◐ |
| Pricing/commit management (Dedicated contracts, capacity commits) | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (read) | ◐ |
| Dedicated capacity admin (GPU pools, autoscaling policy) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ (if granted at project/dedicated scope) | ✅ (read) | ◐ |
| Audit log access (view in Console) | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ◐ (project events only) | ✅ (read, if granted) | ✅ |
| Audit log export configuration (SIEM/exporter) | ◐ (see SoD note) | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ |
| Data access / content access (prompts, completions) | ◐ (depending on product configuration) | ❌ | ❌ | ◐ (project scope only) | ◐ (project scope only) | ◐ |
| Break-glass / emergency elevation | ❌ (not self-service) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ (time-bounded; approval required) |

Important: The table above is intentionally high-level. Actual enforcement is action-by-action per the policy bundle and the service’s permission checks.

---

## Separation of duties (SoD) guidance
### Required SoD principles for enterprise-ready baseline
1) **Billing vs Security are separate by default.**
   - Billing Admin cannot configure SSO or audit export.
   - Security Admin cannot modify payment methods or invoices.

2) **Audit log export is treated as security-sensitive.**
   - Default approach: **Security Admin** owns audit log export configuration and access, not Billing Admin.
   - Rationale: audit exports can contain security-relevant metadata (actors, role IDs, decision reasons) and are commonly used for incident response.

3) **No single non-Org role should combine: identity config + billing config.**
   - If a customer requests this for operational reasons, treat it as a custom role request with documented risk acceptance.

4) **Support impersonation is never a standing customer role.**
   - It is an internal Redwood workflow with explicit approvals, time bounds, and audit evidence.

### Recommended minimum admin set (enterprise)
For most customers, we recommend assigning:
- 1–2 users: **Org Admin** (kept small)
- 1–2 users: **Billing Admin**
- 2+ users: **Security Admin**
- Remaining engineers: **Developer** (project-scoped)
- Stakeholders/auditors: **Read-only**

---

## Role definitions (detailed)
### 1) Org Admin
**Intent:** Full administrative control of the org, including user and role management.

**Typical personas:** Head of Platform, IT admin (for smaller orgs), primary enterprise admin.

**Default includes:**
- Create/update org settings
- Manage memberships
- Assign default roles
- Create/manage projects
- Manage most operational settings (with tier constraints)

**Explicit cautions:**
- Org Admin is powerful; keep membership small.
- Org Admin should not be used for day-to-day engineering work if Developer + Security Admin cover needs.

**Tier notes:**
- Dedicated capacity admin actions may also require a Dedicated entitlement; role alone is not sufficient.

---

### 2) Billing Admin
**Intent:** Handle financial operations without granting identity, security, or production access.

**Typical personas:** Finance ops, procurement lead, operations manager.

**Default includes:**
- View invoices and usage summaries
- Update billing profile details
- Manage payment method (where supported)
- View commitments and contract-related usage reporting

**Explicit excludes:**
- Cannot configure SSO/SAML/OIDC
- Cannot export audit logs
- Cannot manage API keys
- Cannot change Dedicated scaling policies

---

### 3) Security Admin
**Intent:** Configure and monitor security posture for the org.

**Typical personas:** Security engineering, IAM owner, GRC/security operations.

**Default includes:**
- Configure SSO/SAML/OIDC settings
- Configure security policies available in the tier (e.g., session TTL constraints, API key restrictions where applicable)
- View audit logs org-wide
- Configure audit log export (SIEM integration) and validate exporter health

**Explicit excludes:**
- Cannot manage billing payment methods/invoices
- Should not be the only role holder capable of granting themselves broader access (avoid single-person control)

**Notes:**
- For compliance evidence, Security Admin actions should be heavily audit-logged (actor, role IDs, policy version, allow/deny).

---

### 4) Developer (project-scoped)
**Intent:** Build and operate application resources within a project without org-wide administrative control.

**Typical personas:** Application engineers, ML engineers, MLOps.

**Default includes (project scope):**
- Manage API keys for the project (create/rotate/revoke/list)
- Configure model routing/rollouts for the project (within constraints)
- View project usage and operational metrics
- View project audit events (where enabled)

**Explicit excludes:**
- Cannot invite/remove users at the org level
- Cannot configure SSO
- Cannot configure billing
- Cannot configure org-wide audit export

---

### 5) Read-only
**Intent:** Allow visibility without the ability to change state.

**Typical personas:** Auditors, executives, support managers (customer side), incident reviewers.

**Default includes:**
- View dashboards and configuration in Console (read-only)
- View audit logs (read-only) if explicitly enabled for the org/project

**Explicit excludes:**
- No create/update/delete actions
- No key management
- No billing changes

---

### 6) Support (Impersonation / Break-glass) — internal Redwood only
**Intent:** Enable urgent diagnostics and customer support workflows under strict controls.

**Properties:**
- Time-bounded elevated session (break-glass)
- Approval requirements (per internal policy)
- Alerts/monitoring on usage
- Separate audit events for “elevation granted” and “impersonation used”

**Customer visibility:**
- Customers should see relevant audit events and, where applicable, be able to restrict/disable support access in Private deployments (based on contract and product capability).

Reference: “Support break-glass access” policy.

---

## Examples: common enterprise setups
### Example A: Finance-only access
- Group: `finance-billing-admins` → Role: **Billing Admin** (org scope)
- Outcome: finance can manage invoices/payment but cannot access SSO, API keys, or audit export.

### Example B: Security team controls audit export and SSO
- Group: `security-iam-admins` → Role: **Security Admin** (org scope)
- Outcome: security can configure SSO and audit export; cannot change payment method.

### Example C: Engineers are least-privilege per project
- Group: `eng-llm-app-foo` → Role: **Developer** (project: `foo`)
- Group: `eng-llm-app-bar` → Role: **Developer** (project: `bar`)
- Outcome: engineers can rotate keys and manage rollouts only in their projects.

### Example D: Dedicated operations split (recommended)
- Org Admin: limited
- Dedicated capacity admin actions handled either by:
  - Org Admin (small set), or
  - A custom “Dedicated Operator” role (if customer requires delegation) that does not include billing or SSO

---

## SSO group/claim mapping guidance
### Recommended mapping strategy
1) Prefer **IdP groups** → **RBAC roles** mapping.
2) Use **separate groups for each default role**.
3) Use **project-scoped groups** for Developer roles when possible.

### Group naming conventions (recommended)
Use stable, descriptive names. Examples:
- `redwood-{orgSlug}-org-admin`
- `redwood-{orgSlug}-security-admin`
- `redwood-{orgSlug}-billing-admin`
- `redwood-{orgSlug}-read-only`
- `redwood-{orgSlug}-project-{projectSlug}-developer`

### Claim formats we support (typical)
Exact claim name is customer-dependent; common patterns:
- OIDC: `groups` claim contains a list of group strings
- SAML: `memberOf` attribute contains group strings

### Mapping rules (examples)
- If claim contains `redwood-acme-security-admin` → assign **Security Admin** at org scope
- If claim contains `redwood-acme-project-search-developer` → assign **Developer** for project `search`

### SCIM considerations
If SCIM provisioning is enabled, group membership changes should propagate quickly; however:
- Expect eventual consistency; avoid workflows that require instantaneous revocation without compensating controls.
- RBAC v2 policy evaluation and role assignment caches must be invalidated; if you suspect staleness, confirm with the “role assignment updated” audit event and cache metrics.

### Anti-patterns to avoid
- **Single “admins” group** mapped to Org Admin for convenience.
- **Mixing finance and security users** into the same group.
- **Project groups that also grant org-wide roles** (hard to reason about during audits).

---

## Operational notes
### Auditing expectations
All role assignment changes and all authorization decisions for sensitive actions should emit audit log events that include:
- actor identity
- effective role IDs
- policy bundle version
- decision (allow/deny)
- reason code

### Break-glass and incident workflows
- Do not grant standing elevated roles to on-call users to “save time.”
- Use break-glass/time-bounded elevation per policy; ensure approvals and monitoring are configured.

---

## Change management
- Changes to default roles require Security review (Marcus Lin) and GRC alignment (Olga Petrov).
- Any change that weakens SoD (especially combining billing + security export + identity config) requires explicit risk review by the CISO (Dr. Aisha Rahman).

---

## FAQ
**Q: Do you support custom roles?**
A: RBAC v2 is designed to support custom roles; default roles are the recommended baseline. Custom roles should be created only after the permission inventory is understood and the customer can validate access review processes.

**Q: Why is audit log export under Security Admin and not Billing Admin?**
A: Audit exports are used for security monitoring/incident response and can include security-relevant metadata. Separating this from billing reduces misuse risk and aligns with common enterprise SoD expectations.

**Q: Can Read-only users see prompts/completions?**
A: By default, Read-only is for configuration and audit visibility. Access to content depends on product configuration and the specific “content read” permissions granted; treat content access as sensitive and prefer project scoping.
